rungs: It changes with chronological age, or was trained to.
In people followed forward, it predicts death or disease beyond what age alone does.
Genetics (MR) or a direct manipulation asks whether the marker itself drives the outcome.
A randomized trial has moved it.
A randomized trial moved it AND changed hard outcomes. Only this rung makes a surrogate.

markers.name: Horvath pan-tissue clock
markers.link: DNA methylation age measures the work of an "epigenetic maintenance system"; a clock running ahead of the calendar would mean that system is wearing out faster.
ev: multi-tissue predictor of age
Built to predict calendar age across 51 tissues; near zero in stem cells.
highly heritable measure of age acceleration
Running ahead of the calendar is heritable, so it is not just noise.
A 5-year higher Δage is associated with a 21% higher mortality risk

Four cohorts of older people; 16% after adjusting for health, IQ, class and APOE. The abstract says "DNA methylation age"; the paper computed it with the Horvath and Hannum clocks (full text, not archived).

sources.title: DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types.
DNA methylation age of blood predicts all-cause mortality in later life.

markers.name: Hannum blood clock
markers.link: Each person's methylome ages at a rate, and a faster rate is a faster-aging body.
ev: measures the rate at which an individual's methylome ages
656 people, aged 19 to 101; the rate differs by sex and gene variants.
A 5-year higher Δage is associated with a 21% higher mortality risk

Four cohorts of older people; 16% after adjusting for health, IQ, class and APOE. The abstract says "DNA methylation age"; the paper computed it with the Horvath and Hannum clocks (full text, not archived).

sources.title: Genome-wide methylation profiles reveal quantitative views of human aging rates.
DNA methylation age of blood predicts all-cause mortality in later life.

markers.name: PhenoAge (DNAm)
markers.link: Trained on a clinical score that predicts death, not on calendar age, so the methylation it picks up should be the part that matters for lifespan.
ev: epmc-10_18632_aging_101414.json
including all-cause mortality
Predicts all-cause mortality, cancers, physical function, Alzheimer's.
did not lead to significant changes in biological age estimates measured by various DNAm clocks including PhenoAge and GrimAge
Two years of 25% calorie restriction (CALERIE, randomized, n = 220) did not move it.

sources.title: An epigenetic biomarker of aging for lifespan and healthspan.
Effect of long-term caloric restriction on DNA methylation measures of biological aging in healthy adults from the CALERIE trial.

markers.name: GrimAge
markers.link: Methylation stand-ins for seven plasma proteins and for smoking pack-years, combined into a "predictor of lifespan".
ev: epmc-10_18632_aging_101684.json
time-to-death (Cox regression P=2.0E-75)
The strongest death predictor among the clocks of its time.
did not lead to significant changes in biological age estimates measured by various DNAm clocks including PhenoAge and GrimAge
CALERIE did not move it either.

sources.title: DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan.
Effect of long-term caloric restriction on DNA methylation measures of biological aging in healthy adults from the CALERIE trial.

markers.name: DunedinPACE
markers.link: Not "how old" but "how fast": trained on 20 years of decline in 19 organ measures in one 1972–73 birth cohort.
ev: epmc-10_7554_eLife_73420.json
was associated with morbidity, disability, and mortality
Also adds prediction beyond GrimAge; high test-retest reliability.
CALERIE intervention slowed the pace of aging, as measured by the DunedinPACE DNAm algorithm
The only clock here moved in a randomized trial, and the paper says "Treatment effect sizes were small".
will require trials with long-term follow-up to establish effects of intervention on primary healthy-aging endpoints
No trial has shown that slowing it changes disease or death. The CALERIE authors say so themselves.

sources.title: DunedinPACE, a DNA methylation biomarker of the pace of aging.
Effect of long-term caloric restriction on DNA methylation measures of biological aging in healthy adults from the CALERIE trial.

markers.name: Proteomic aging clock (204 proteins)
markers.link: The blood's protein mix shifts with age across many organ systems, so a protein age ahead of the calendar flags a body ahead of the calendar.
ev: as well as with multimorbidity and all-cause mortality risk
UK Biobank n = 45,441; 18 chronic diseases; age prediction held up in China and Finland.

sources.title: Proteomic aging clock predicts mortality and risk of common age-related diseases in diverse populations.

markers.name: Organ-specific proteomic ages
markers.link: Organs age at different speeds in one person; proteins shed by one organ date that organ.
ev: Accelerated organ aging confers 20-50% higher mortality risk
About 20% of people have one organ aging fast; accelerated heart age raises heart failure risk by 250%.

sources.title: Organ aging signatures in the plasma proteome track health and disease.

markers.name: Telomere length
markers.link: Telomeres shorten with each division, so short telomeres were read as a worn-out body and long ones as a young one.
ev: epmc-10_1001_jamaoncol_2016_5945.json
longer telomeres increase risk for several cancers but reduce risk for some non-neoplastic diseases
MR (420,081 cases): genetically longer telomeres raise glioma, lung adenocarcinoma and melanoma risk and lower heart disease risk. Longer is not simply better.

sources.title: Association Between Telomere Length and Risk of Cancer and Non-Neoplastic Diseases: A Mendelian Randomization Study.

markers.name: Senescent cells (p16Ink4a+)
markers.link: Cells that stop dividing but keep secreting inflammatory signals pile up with age and damage the tissue around them.
ev: epmc-10_1038_nature16932.json
extended median lifespan in both male and female mice of two distinct genetic backgrounds
Killing p16+ cells with a transgene, from one year of age: the strongest causal result in this table. It is in mice, with a genetic switch no drug has.

sources.title: Naturally occurring p16(Ink4a)-positive cells shorten healthy lifespan.

markers.name: Clonal hematopoiesis (CHIP)
markers.link: Blood stem cells with cancer-linked mutations take over a share of the blood, and those cells may drive vessel disease as well as cancer.
ev: epmc-10_1056_NEJMoa1408617.json
epmc-10_1056_NEJMoa1408617.json
an increase in all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.1 to 1.8)
The authors say "possibly due to" heart disease: a hypothesis, not a test.

sources.title: Age-related clonal hematopoiesis associated with adverse outcomes.
sources.journal: The New England journal of medicine

markers.name: C-reactive protein (CRP)
markers.link: "Inflammaging": low-grade inflammation rises with age and drives disease.
ev: epmc-pmid-20031199.json
non-vascular mortality
In 160,309 people, each SD of log CRP carried an RR of about 1.5 for vascular and for non-vascular death.
epmc-10_1136_bmj_d548.json
unlikely to be even a modest causal factor in coronary heart disease
MR in 194,418 people: CRP marks heart risk, it doesn't cause it. A gauge, not a lever.

sources.title: C-reactive protein concentration and risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and mortality: an individual participant meta-analysis.
Association between C reactive protein and coronary heart disease: mendelian randomisation analysis based on individual participant data.

markers.name: Frailty index
markers.link: Aging is the accumulation of many small failures, so the share of deficits a person has reflects how close they are to death, whichever deficits they are.
ev: deficits accumulated at 3% per year
In elderly Canadians.
serves as an important prognostic factor for life expectancy
The founding paper; widely re-tested since (not archived here).

sources.title: Accumulation of deficits as a proxy measure of aging.

markers.name: Gait speed
markers.link: Walking speed integrates heart, lungs, muscle, nerves and balance, so it reads the whole system at once.
ev: pooled hazard ratio per 0.1 m/s, 0.88
9 cohorts, 34,485 people aged 65+.

sources.title: Gait speed and survival in older adults.

markers.name: Grip strength
markers.link: Muscle strength stands for the body's reserve.
ev: epmc-pmid-25982160.json
hazard ratio per 5 kg reduction in grip strength 1.16
PURE, 139,691 people in 17 countries.
epmc-pmid-25982160.json
to test whether improvement in strength reduces mortality
The authors' own open question: nobody has shown that getting stronger moves the death rate.

sources.title: Prognostic value of grip strength: findings from the Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology (PURE) study.

markers.name: Cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max, METs)
markers.link: Peak oxygen use sets how much the whole body can do.
ev: epmc-10_1001_jamanetworkopen_2018_3605.json
adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.20
Elite vs low fitness, 122,007 patients referred for treadmill tests; no upper limit seen. Retrospective, and people who were already sick were sent for testing.

sources.title: Association of Cardiorespiratory Fitness With Long-term Mortality Among Adults Undergoing Exercise Treadmill Testing.

markers.name: LDL cholesterol
markers.link: Not an aging marker. It is here as the template: what a validated surrogate looks like.
ev: epmc-pmid-21067804.json
each 1·0 mmol/L reduction reducing the annual rate of these major vascular events by just over a fifth
26 randomized trials, about 170,000 people. On FDA's surrogate table.

sources.title: Efficacy and safety of more intensive lowering of LDL cholesterol: a meta-analysis of data from 170,000 participants in 26 randomised trials.

markers.name: Systolic blood pressure
markers.link: Not an aging marker; a second validated surrogate.
ev: epmc-10_1056_NEJMoa1511939.json
death from any cause
SPRINT: aiming for <120 instead of <140 mm Hg cut major events and deaths from all causes. On FDA's surrogate table.

sources.title: A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control.
sources.journal: The New England journal of medicine

markers.name: HbA1c
markers.link: Not an aging marker. It is here as the warning: an accepted surrogate, moved hard, and more people died.
ev: epmc-10_1056_NEJMoa0802743.json
increased mortality and did not significantly reduce major cardiovascular events
ACCORD: aiming for HbA1c <6.0% in high-risk type 2 diabetes raised deaths (HR 1.22). HbA1c is still on FDA's surrogate table for diabetes drugs.

sources.title: Effects of intensive glucose lowering in type 2 diabetes.
sources.journal: The New England journal of medicine
